items.title: Weak 3.7-magnitude earthquake strikes off Sandakan, no tsunami threat to Malaysia
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 18 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.7 on the Richter scale was detected about 88 kilometres north of Sandakan, Sabah at 10.30pm yesterday. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement on Facebook, said the earthquake occurred at coordinates 6.6 degrees North and 118.3 degrees East. It said the epicentre was about 354 kilometres south of Palawan, Philippines and 88 kilometres north of Sandakan, at a depth of 392 kilometres.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for northern states, Sabah and Sarawak until noon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning covering multiple states across the country, cautioning that thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected until 12 noon today. In the northern peninsula, the entire state of Perlis is under warning, along with several districts in Kedah, including Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Pendang, Pokok Sena, Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Kuala Muda, Yan and Baling. Penang is also affected in its entirety, while Perak faces widespread impact across Hulu Perak, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah and Kuala Kangsar.

items.title: Johor Plantations' palm oil complex opens new growth avenue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Plantations Group Bhd's move into higher-value downstream palm oil products through its Integrated Sustainable Palm Oil Complex (iSPOC) could open a new earnings growth avenue from financial year 2027 (FY27). Apex Securities Bhd, which has initiated coverage on the company, said the complex would mark Johor Plantations' transition beyond bulk crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel production into value-added palm-based products. Apex Securities said a tighter supply outlook would benefit Johor Plantations given its predominantly upstream earnings exposure.

items.title: Ex-SD Guthrie supervisor gets RM127,600 after dismissal over sexual harassment claims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Industrial Court has awarded RM127,600 to a former SD Guthrie Bhd field supervisor after ruling that allegations of sexual harassment, threats and insubordination used to justify his dismissal were not proven. Industrial Court chairman Augustine Anthony criticised the company's disciplinary process, describing some of the charges against E. S. Munusamy as an "afterthought". The court also rejected allegations that Munusamy later threatened to murder the complainant and burn him or his living quarters.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office backs AGC view, says won’t gazette April 19 proclamation on Ruler
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 18 — The Negeri Sembilan government will not take any action to gazette or enforce the April 19, 2026 proclamation regarding the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar, the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s (SUK) office said in a statement last night. It said the state government abided by the AGC’s view that members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMKN) had no jurisdiction, authority, or power under the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 to announce the proclamation. Meanwhile, the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) reiterated that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and chairman of the DKU.

items.title: Passenger dies after medical emergency on Malaysia Airlines flight to Sydney
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A passenger died on board a Sydney-bound Malaysia Airlines flight after suffering a critical medical emergency mid-air on Wednesday. Malaysia Airlines confirmed that the passenger on board flight MH141 from Kuala Lumpur to Sydney could not be revived despite immediate emergency medical intervention by crew members and qualified medical personnel on board, news.com.au reported. The flight departed Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday morning and touched down at Sydney Airport at 7.43pm local time.

items.title: Yen weak ahead of BoJ decision, rate hike expected
items.summary: The yen fell 0.1 per cent to 156.19 yen per dollar, resuming its decline after snapping a three-day losing streak on Thursday as traders prepare for the Japanese central bank to lift interest rates to the highest level in more than three decades. Against the euro, the yen was 0.2 per cent weaker at 179.3000 yen. The euro was flat at US$1.1478.

items.title: Oil prices fall 1pct on hopes of limited supply disruptions
items.summary: HOUSTON: Oil prices fell about one per cent, extending losses for a third session, but stayed above US$100 on Friday, as hopes of alternative ways for barrels from the Middle East to reach markets outweighed concerns about strikes between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis. Brent crude futures fell US$1.01, or one per cent, to US$103.77 a barrel by 0020 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate futures fell US$1.03, or one per cent, to US$100.88 a barrel. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said that crude should be flowing through the pipeline within days.

items.title: #NSTviral: Sea turtle makes surprise visit behind woman's home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A woman got an unexpected visitor when a sea turtle came ashore at night and made its way onto the sandy area behind her home. In a Threads post by @nvdivsharheera , she shared several pictures showing the turtle just a few metres from her house. In response to questions, the woman said the turtle was believed to have come ashore at 8pm and spent several hours digging in the sand.

items.title: New-generation MyKad drops Touch ’n Go feature, focuses on security, says NRD
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The new-generation MyKad, which started being issued yesterday, no longer comes with the Touch ’n Go facility. In a social media post, the National Registration Department (NRD) said users can still access the service through the Touch ’n Go eWallet or a separate Touch ’n Go card. “For users who wish to continue using Touch ’n Go services, the facility can be accessed through the Touch ’n Go eWallet or a separate Touch ’n Go card,” it said.

items.title: FT Pardons Board convenes at Istana Negara amid talk of Najib’s petition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh and Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar have both reached Istana Negara here for a suddenly-scheduled Pardons Board meeting this morning. The meeting is shrouded by speculation that the board is being reconvened to determined pardon application of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which had been deferred during the previous meeting on Sept 11. Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.

items.title: Girl kicked, pushed by friends after taunting incident in Miri
items.summary: District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said police received a report concerning the video, which showed several boys and girls involved in a fight. He said the incident occurred around 5pm on Wednesday in front of one of the children's houses. "Police have identified all seven children involved in the video, aged between eight and 13.

items.title: Service and dedication to fairness: True legacy of judicial leadership
items.summary: LETTERS: I read with deep appreciation the NST report "CJ: Judges' Legacies Make a Judiciary". I could not agree more with the profound observation by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh: "A judiciary is built not merely of marble and mahogany, but on the legacies of our judicial predecessors. The Chief Justice's tribute to four former leaders of our judiciary — Tun Mohamed Eusoff Chin, Tun Mohamed Dzaiddin Abdullah, Tun Abdul Hamid Mohamad, and Tun Siti Norma Yaakob — reminds us that legacies are made not by titles, but by service.

items.title: Sarawak and Selangor bear the brunt as 34 stations log ‘Unhealthy’ API levels in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated significantly this morning, with 34 monitoring stations nationwide recording “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 8.30am, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data. Sarawak and Selangor hardest hit Sarawak emerged as the most affected state overall, with eight monitoring stations entering the unhealthy range. Selangor recorded the highest concentration of polluted areas in Peninsular Malaysia, with six stations logging unhealthy air quality.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh, A-G arrive at Istana Negara ahead of Pardons Board meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar arrived at Istana Negara this morning ahead of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting. The meeting comes amid reports that the board will reconvene today with a single item on the agenda regarding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application. The application was deferred at the 63rd Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting on Sept 11, with consideration postponed to a subsequent meeting.

items.title: Johan Setia records highest API reading at 198
items.summary: Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed 34 stations recorded unhealthy API readings, while 31 recorded moderate readings and three recorded good readings. Putrajaya recorded 173, while Tasek Ipoh in Perak recorded 172. Cheras recorded 166, while Alor Gajah in Melaka recorded 165.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar as oil prices ease
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and a basket of major currencies on Friday, supported by improved market sentiment as easing Middle East crude oil supply concerns lifted risk appetite. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market sentiment was lifted after Saudi Arabia reportedly began restoring its damaged East-West pipeline, while tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz continued, easing immediate concerns over supply. "As a result, Brent crude oil prices fell 0.95 per cent to US$104.82 per barrel, while US Treasury yields declined, with the two- and 10-year notes falling seven basis points each to 4.67 per cent and 4.94 per cent, respectively.

items.title: University student to be charged over Kluang crash that killed four
items.summary: KLUANG: A 19-year-old university student is expected to be charged at the magistrate's court this morning over a reckless driving incident that claimed the lives of four family members in June. The suspect will face charges before magistrate Nurasidah A Rahman under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for driving recklessly and dangerously along Jalan Renggam-Simpang Renggam. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh had previously said the investigation paper concerning the suspect had been referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers.

items.title: South Korea to extend fuel tax cut through November amid price burdens
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea will extend its fuel tax cut scheme by another two months through November to ease price burdens on the public amid protracted tensions in West Asia, the Finance Ministry said Friday. Yonhap reported the finance and economy minister said the decision was made during an economy-related ministers' meeting chaired by finance minister Koo Yun-cheol, citing the need to ease the public's burden from fuel costs. "We have decided to maintain the current tax cut scheme, considering the country's capacity to address a possible increase in oil price volatility," the finance ministry said in a release.

items.title: Australia's central bank chief warns inflation risks appear to be materialising
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's top central banker said on Friday some of the upside risks to inflation flagged by policymakers appeared to be materialising, with the Middle East conflict and the artificial intelligence boom putting upward pressure on prices. Appearing before lawmakers, Michele Bullock, governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), said a key question facing policymakers at its policy meeting this month would be whether three rate hikes this year would be sufficient to bring inflation back to target in a reasonable time. The RBA held interest rates steady at 4.35 per cent for a second meeting in August, but it singled out the Middle East war and a global data centre investment boom as key risks to inflation.

items.title: Iran strikes, detains oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Friday they struck an oil tanker sailing under the Togolese flag in the Strait of Hormuz, state news agency IRNA reported. Teheran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the United States and Israel struck Iran in late February. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) announced Thursday a "security incident in the Strait of Hormuz, 16 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman."

items.title: Bank of Japan set to raise interest rates to 31-year high
items.summary: But the Federal Reserve's rate hike on Wednesday and prospects of another move later this year have piled pressure on the BoJ to keep pace, as a widening of an already big US-Japan rate gap could weaken the yen and lift inflation through higher import costs, analysts say. At the two-day meeting ending on Friday, the BoJ is set to raise its policy rate to 1.25 per cent from one per cent. A hike to 1.25 per cent would bring the BoJ's policy rate to levels unseen since 1995.

items.title: Journalists' Syndicate: Sick and injured journalists in Gaza face harsh conditions and need medical evacuation
items.summary: RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Journalists' Syndicate said that journalists and media workers in the Gaza Strip are facing exceptional and harsh conditions amid the ongoing genocidal war carried out by Israeli occupation forces. The Syndicate said that journalists and media workers in the Gaza Strip are working in an extremely dangerous environment amid shelling and displacement, deteriorating humanitarian conditions, the collapse of large parts of the healthcare system, and shortages of medicines and medical supplies. It stressed that the issue of sick and injured journalists whose conditions require urgent medical evacuation outside the Gaza Strip has become an urgent humanitarian and human rights issue, particularly in cases involving serious neurological injuries, limb injuries, chronic illnesses, or requiring specialised surgery and rehabilitation.

items.title: Malaysian bonds, ringgit face fresh Fed & BoJ rate headwinds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's ringgit and bond market may come under renewed pressure if the US Federal Reserve resumes monetary tightening. This could fuel capital outflows and complicate Bank Negara Malaysia's interest-rate policy, economists said. Tighter US monetary policy could raise funding costs and global market volatility, he added.

items.title: Malaysia's India trade review must tackle structural barriers: Economists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's review of its trade framework with India should focus on removing structural barriers and helping Malaysian companies gain greater access to its market, economists said. Johari said India had stressed the importance of a more balanced trading relationship, noting that Malaysia currently recorded a sizeable trade surplus with India. In 2025, Malaysia recorded a trade surplus of RM25.37 billion with India, with total bilateral trade reaching RM79.33 billion, down five per cent from RM83.5 billion in 2024.

items.title: KKIA runway reopens after rectification works
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Flight operations at Kota Kinabalu International Airport (KKIA) can resume after the airport's runway was reopened at 11.30pm yeserday following final safety checks, Malaysia Airports said. In an update on its official Facebook page, Malaysia Airports said flight operations could resume following the reopening. Malaysia Airports also advised passengers travelling to and from KKIA to check with their respective airlines for the latest flight status updates.

items.title: France arrests far-right policeman suspected of terrorist plot
items.summary: PARIS: A policeman who follows "a violent radical far-right ideology" has been arrested in France on suspicion of plotting a terrorist attack, sources told AFP late on Thursday. Confirming a report by the TF1/LCI broadcaster, a judicial source said that the man was also suspected of having manufactured weapons, among other crimes. A separate source close to the case told AFP that the police officer, aged 35, was "apprehended on the street" on August 23.

items.title: 5 reports lodged over kicking of incense pot
items.summary: BERA: Five police reports have been lodged by Orang Asli villagers following a viral incident involving an enforcement team member who allegedly kicked a burning incense pot at Kampung Pathir here on Sept 15. The incident occurred during a joint enforcement operation at the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve (Ramsar) site. District police chief Superintendent Zulkiflee Nazir said the reports were lodged by Orang Asli villagers living near the Tasek Bera between Sept 15 and Wednesday.

items.title: Pahang govt ready to help Tasek Bera Orang Asli, but needs details [WATCH]
items.summary: KUANTAN: The Pahang government is prepared to assist Orang Asli living near Tasek Bera, but delays in providing a list of residents in the settlements have hampered efforts to help them. Pahang Islamic Religious Affairs, Rural Development and Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad said there were more than seven villages near the lake, but only one had submitted the required list. He said during a visit to several Orang Asli settlements near the lake on Aug 3, that he had assured the villagers that the state government wanted to help them continue earning a livelihood.

items.title: NYT alleges Microsoft, OpenAI knew using news content was theft
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: OpenAI committed "an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions" when it used millions of news articles to train its artificial intelligence models, the New York Times alleged in a court document unsealed on Thursday. The newspaper sued OpenAI and Microsoft three years ago in New York federal court for allegedly stealing its copyrighted material to train OpenAI's flagship model, ChatGPT. Microsoft first invested in OpenAI in 2019.

items.title: Ice, fans and cooling pads: How Malaysia’s chicken farmers are beating El Niño heat
items.summary: Heat poses a far more serious challenge, and one that farmers cannot simply keep outside the door. A prolonged spell of extreme heat could affect how quickly chickens grow, how much farmers lose and how well they perform. Keeping the heat out Malay Mail recently visited Muzamri’s farm, where the broiler farmer and chairman of the Selangor Poultry Farmers Association has spent 26 years raising chickens.

items.title: N.Korea leader's sister blasts US drills, threatens 'more offensive' response
items.summary: SEOUL: The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un accused the United States of escalating regional tensions through frequent military drills and warned of a "more offensive" response from Pyongyang, according to a statement published by state media Friday. "The present situation, in which new records are set in terms of practical action hostile toward the DPRK, stresses the need to break records in our responsive action, proportional or more offensive in its nature," the KCNA news agency quoted Kim Yo Jong as saying, using North Korea's official name, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. "I remind the enemy once again that if it is judged that the supreme interests of our nation and its military sovereignty and security environment in the region have been seriously violated by their military maneuovers," Kim went on, North Korea's military will "mobilise all means available to cope with it."

items.title: US F-16 warplane crashes in Michigan
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A Texas-based US military F-16 fighter jet crashed Thursday during a training mission in Michigan, with the pilot able to eject, the unit to which the aircraft belonged said. "A Texas Air National Guard F-16 Fighting Falcon assigned to the 149th Fighter Wing...crashed during a routine training mission" near Traverse City, the unit said in a statement on its Facebook page. Grand Traverse County Emergency Management in Michigan said on Facebook that an evacuation order is "in effect due to a plane crash."

items.title: Takaichi keeps key ministers
items.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi yesterday retained key ministers in a cabinet reshuffle that seeks to shore up political support to push through her flagship spending plans amid jittery financial markets. In her first reshuffle since taking office last October, Takaichi kept Satsuki Katayama as finance minister, a move that provides continuity in Japan's exchange-rate policy. Takachi also appointed Hiroshi Nakatsuka from the Japan Innovation Party as minister in charge of deregulation.

items.title: Indonesia to begin e-commerce tax collection
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia will begin making e-commerce platforms collect income taxes from sellers starting Oct 1, a month earlier than previously announced, local media reported yesterday, citing the tax chief. The move reverses a delay ordered by the previous finance minister and follows a shake-up at the top of the Finance Ministry this week. They are ready, we are ready," Indonesian Finance Ministry's Tax Department head, Bimo Wijayanto, said, according to CNBC Indonesia, adding that the collection would begin Oct 1.

items.title: Mada sounds warning as Kedah dam levels fall to 35pc
items.summary: Water levels at three irrigation dams have dropped to an average of 35.76 per cent, posing a major challenge to padi farmers ahead of the second planting season. The Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) said yesterday water levels at the Pedu Dam, Ahning Dam and Muda Dam were at 36.99 per cent, 44.33 per cent and 11.88 per cent, respectively. "Up to Sept 16, pre-saturation progress had reached 100 per cent, land preparation at 99 per cent and planting at 98.4 per cent, whereas the harvest rate stood at 9.3 per cent," it said.

items.title: Tok Saimah's secret to longevity is healthy diet
items.summary: At 102, Saimah Sajiman has no complicated formula for staying healthy. Fondly known as Tok Saimah, the centenarian from Kampung Rahmat, Sri Lalang, believes that maintaining a healthy diet, particularly choosing boiled food over fried or oily dishes, is among the practices that have helped her stay healthy. "It is not that I do not eat fried food, but I prefer boiled food such as 'sayur bening' (clear vegetable soup), 'ikan pais' (steamed fish with spices) and traditional village 'ulam' (vegetable salads)," she said at her home.

items.title: 3.7-magnitude quake detected 88km north of Sandakan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A weak earthquake measuring 3.7 on the Richter scale was detected about 88km north of Sandakan, Sabah, at 10.30pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement on Facebook, said the earthquake occurred at 6.6 degrees North and 118.3 degrees East. MetMalaysia said the earthquake posed no tsunami threat to Malaysia.

items.title: AGC: Exco statement has no legal effect, move to gazette or implement proclamation on N. Sembilan Yamtuan’s removal invalid, unconstitutional
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) said the Negeri Sembilan state executive council’s media statement or announcement has no legal effect as its members had no jurisdiction, authority or power under the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 to make it. The AGC said there was also no legal basis for the state executive council members to rely on the April 19, 2026 proclamation for their announcement, adding that any move to gazette or implement the proclamation would be invalid and unconstitutional. In a statement today, the AGC said it had taken note of the document titled “Media Statement of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council — Decision of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council Meeting No.

items.title: Second body recovered as search continues for missing Pulau Ketam anglers
items.summary: Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) operations officer, Maritime Lieutenant Mohd Syafiq Sazali said a local fishing boat spotted a man’s body floating at 4.26 pm. Mohd Syafiq added that the latest recovery was about two nautical miles from where the first victim, Mohd Shahril Abd Rahman, was found yesterday. Khairul said the family is hopeful Muhammad Ridzuan is safe.

items.title: KL to add 49ha of green spaces as city moves to protect open areas, says Hannah Yeoh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will create nearly 49 hectares of new recreational spaces and public parks across the capital, as part of efforts to expand the city’s network of green areas and recreational facilities. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the strategic initiative included pre-development works and the utilisation of Department of Irrigation and Drainage reserves along Sungai Bunus and Kolam Ayer Panas. “Our main aim under this initiative is not merely to create new recreational spaces, but to ensure that every valuable open and green space in Kuala Lumpur is legally gazetted and protected,” she said after inspecting the Bunus Flood Retention Pond here today.

items.title: Malaysian woman, 40, dies during scuba dive in Bali’s Crystal Bay
items.summary: BALI, Sept 17 — A 40-year-old Malaysian woman died while scuba diving in the waters off Crystal Bay, Desa Sakti, Bali, Indonesia, yesterday. According to local media portal BaliNews, Siti Nuraini joined a diving trip with a dive guide, boat captain and several other divers at about 8am. However, concerns arose over her condition when the dive guide, Eugenius Franciso Ray, 33, noticed her coughing after they arrived at their first dive site at Manta Bay.

items.title: Malaysia offers Indonesia aircraft, helicopters to fight forest fires amid haze concerns, says Zahid
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 17 — Malaysia has officially offered assistance to Indonesia in tackling forest fires, including a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft previously deployed to help its neighbour combat similar fires. Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the assistance would also include three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF). “We want to help Indonesia address the problem together,” he said.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysian households using up to 800kWh exempt from AFA, Retail Charge and SST on electricity bills until Dec 31 amid haze, heat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The government has expanded electricity bill protection for domestic users from 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) to 800kWh a month from September to December 31, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in a Facebook post today. He said the measure was an immediate step to ease the cost-of-living pressures faced by households, particularly as haze and hotter weather have driven up electricity consumption in some homes. He said the recent haze and warmer weather had contributed to increased electricity consumption among some households, causing their monthly usage to exceed 600kWh and resulting in unusually higher bills.

items.title: Police probe Simpang Pulai road rage after Mercedes driver allegedly threatened with stick
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — Police are investigating an incident where a car driver was allegedly threatened with a wooden stick on Jalan Ipoh-Gopeng, Simpang Pulai, near here, yesterday. Ipoh district police chief ACP Muhammad Najib Hamzah said today that the incident occurred at 4.56pm when the victim, driving a Mercedes, claimed that his vehicle was forced to the side by a Toyota Vios before a misunderstanding arose after the victim honked at the other vehicle. The incident was also recorded by a dashboard camera (dashcam), he said.

items.title: Ipoh woman loses RM41,215 in online job and fake investment scams
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — A 36-year-old woman lost RM41,215 after falling victim to an online job scam and a non-existent investment scheme recently. Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said the victim received a job offer through WhatsApp on September 13, with rewards offered for completing product evaluation tasks on the Shopee platform. He said the victim was subsequently instructed to make several money transfers to bank accounts provided by the suspect.

items.title: ‘Stare’ case at Kepong restaurant: AGC reviewing technician’s representation over grievous hurt charge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) is still reviewing a representation by a technician seeking reconsideration of a charge of causing grievous hurt to a man in a “stare” incident at a restaurant in Kepong here in May. Deputy Public Prosecutor Adiba Iman Hassan said the representation by second accused Lai Kae Bin was submitted on September 2 and is still under consideration. On May 14, Lai, 33, carpenter Wong Weng Luen, 49, and memorial centre worker Wan Ken Fei, 30, pleaded not guilty to intentionally causing grievous hurt to Andrew Teh Tiek Hua, 49, at a restaurant in Jalan Kepong, Metro Prima, at 2am on May 7.

items.title: IGP: Police DNA lab logs 420 matches, seeks more technology for forensic investigations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The enhancement of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) DNA Analysis Laboratory through a RM11.1 million allocation under the 12th Malaysia Plan (12MP) has enabled PDRM to carry out 420 Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) matching cases, including those involving serious crimes. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, however, said PDRM still required additional logistics, equipment and technology to further strengthen its investigative capabilities and help solve more cases that require forensic analysis. Mohd Khalid said other departments and agencies needing forensic analysis assistance could also use the PDRM Forensic Laboratory’s expertise, adding that the increased allocation would enable the adoption of more new technologies in the future.

items.title: No evidence of established piranha population in Pahang’s Klau Dam yet, says Fisheries Dept
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Department of Fisheries (DOF) said today there is no evidence yet of an established or breeding piranha population in the Klau Dam, Raub, following the catch of a fish suspected to be of the species on August 26. Fisheries director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain said only one such fish had so far been reported caught in the area, while investigations and field monitoring by the Pahang Fisheries Department up to September 15 found no additional catches or related safety incidents. He also said that releasing alien fish species that could become invasive into public waters was irresponsible as it could adversely affect inland aquatic ecosystems, local fish populations and aquatic biodiversity.

items.title: Haze: 30 areas across Malaysia record unhealthy air quality, including Ipoh, PJ, Shah Alam and Kuching
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — A total of 30 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5pm today. According to the Malaysia Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Tasek Ipoh in Perak recorded the highest reading at 188, while three other areas in the state also had unhealthy API readings, namely Seri Manjung (179), Pegoh Ipoh (158) and Taiping (155). In Sarawak, three areas recorded unhealthy readings: Kuching (172), Serian IPD (172) and Samarahan (167).

items.title: Vodus study: Anwar records highest acceptance, first-choice support among PM hopefuls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has emerged as the strongest overall candidate for the prime ministership in a new national study by Vodus Research, recording the highest public acceptance, first-choice support and net acceptance among five prominent prospective candidates. The Malaysia Prime Minister Candidate Study 2026 found that 46 per cent of respondents aware of the candidates said they would accept Anwar as prime minister, while 34 per cent named him as their first choice. His net acceptance score stood at +19 percentage points, also the highest among the five candidates surveyed.

items.title: Army steps up drone surveillance on border routes amid unrest in southern Thailand
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) is using advanced drone technology to strengthen security monitoring in hard-to-reach areas along the Malaysia-Thailand border, particularly in response to the unrest in southern Thailand. Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the technology enabled TDM to overcome the challenges posed by hilly and densely forested terrain, where physical patrols by troops were difficult. Azhan also gave an assurance that border security remained tight, with round-the-clock operations in place.

items.title: KLIA ranks first in Asia for connectivity in OAG Megahubs 2026 ranking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KUL) ranked fourth globally and first among all Asian airports in OAG’s Megahubs 2026 ranking, with connections to 154 destinations, while also topping the Low-Cost Carrier (LCC) Megahubs index with nearly 15,000 possible low-cost connections. OAG, the intelligence partner for global travel, said its annual ranking of global airport connectivity showed Asia Pacific (APAC) dominating the index, with eight airports in the global top 20. According to OAG in a statement, AirAsia operates 34 per cent of total flights at KUL, while Seoul Incheon ranked second in the LCC rankings with connectivity reaching 198 destinations.

items.title: Kota Kinabalu airport runway temporarily closed for rectification works
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 17 — The runway at Kota Kinabalu International Airport has been temporarily closed to facilitate rectification works, Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) said today. In a notice on Facebook, MAHB said a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued over the temporary closure. “The runway will reopen once the necessary safety inspections and clearing works have been completed,” it said.

items.title: Papagomo fails to stay RM280,000 defamation payout to Lim Guan Eng, son
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — The High Court today dismissed an application by Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, to stay the execution of a judgment ordering him to pay RM280,000 in damages to former Penang Chief Minister Lim Guan Eng and his son. On May 19 this year, the court ruled that Wan Muhammad Azri was liable for defamation and ordered him to pay RM280,000 in damages to Guan Eng and Clint Lim Way Chau over the latter's posts alleging that Way Chau was detained in Singapore for purportedly bringing in RM2 million in undeclared cash in 2020. The court ordered the defendant to pay global damages of RM200,000 and costs of RM30,000 to Guan Eng as well as damages of RM80,000 and costs of RM10,000 to the second plaintiff (Way Chau).

items.title: Palm oil mill shut down after pump failure sends effluent into Johor’s Sungai Sembrong
items.summary: KLUANG, Sept 17 — A palm oil mill in Kluang has been identified as the source of pollution in Sungai Sembrong and ordered to halt operations immediately. “Further investigation revealed a pump malfunction at the mill’s effluent treatment pond, causing an overflow of oil-contaminated effluent into Sungai Sembrong. The DoE reminded industries, particularly palm oil mill operators, to strictly comply with requirements under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 and the department’s licensing conditions.

items.title: BPHB unit appointed Bintulu Port operator for 30 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) has appointed Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's (BPHB) wholly-owned subsidiary Bintulu Port Sdn Bhd (BPSB) as an approved port operator for Bintulu Port for 30 years, from September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2056. “The appointment is set out in the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak) (Appointment of Approved Port Operator) Notification, 2026, published in the Sarawak Government Gazette, Part II, dated September 10, 2026. On June 23, 2026, the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development notified BPSB that the government had approved in principle the appointment of BPSB as the approved port operator for Bintulu Port under Section 12(2)(a) of the Port Authorities Ordinance, 1961.

items.title: PMO says letter claiming Cabinet approval for PLUS highway widening is fake
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 17 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) today said that a letter dated July 17, 2026, claiming that Cabinet approval had been given for a proposed Private Finance Initiative (PFI) project to widen the North-South Expressway (PLUS) is fake. In a statement today, PMO stressed that the Prime Minister had never issued or signed the letter and denied any connection with the document or the purported approval. “PMO has lodged a police report over the forgery of the document and the misuse of the Prime Minister’s name and PMO’s official identity.

items.title: Critics of Anwar should back their words with action, says PKR Youth chief
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 17 — PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim has hit out at those criticising Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying some were quick to make political statements but lacked the courage to follow through with their actions. He said while there were political statements suggesting that the country was currently unstable, the government remained committed to ensuring political stability as a foundation for economic stability and, ultimately, the benefit of the people. “Our priority is to ensure political stability because from there, we can ensure economic stability, which will ultimately benefit the people,” he said.

items.title: Melaka assembly dissolution date still undecided, says CM
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 17 — The date for the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly to pave the way for the state election has yet to be set, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said several state administrative matters needed to be resolved first to ensure all plans proceeded smoothly before the assembly was dissolved. The Melaka State Assembly has 28 seats, while the current state government's mandate expires on December 31.
